children.value: This page showcases examples of curricular materials I’ve developed for First-Year Engineering courses at Purdue University. Due to intellectual property considerations, I’ve provided descriptions and sample content rather than full materials.
Project 1: Introduction to Engineering Problem Solving

children.label: Project 1: Introduction to Engineering Problem Solving

children.value: ENGR 131 - Transforming Ideas to Innovation I

A comprehensive module introducing engineering problem-solving methodology using computational thinking. Students learn to break down complex problems, design algorithms, and implement solutions using Python.
Apply systematic problem-solving frameworks to engineering challenges
Decompose complex problems into manageable components
with learning objectives, worked examples, and discussion prompts
with scaffolded exercises building programming skills
progressing from basic to advanced concepts
where students design and implement a solution to a real-world problem
including quizzes, rubrics, and answer keys
— Gradual progression from simple to complex
— Engineering problems relevant to student interests
— Hands-on coding exercises and pair programming
Consistently positive student feedback on clarity and engagement
Project 2: Data Analysis for Engineering Decisions

children.label: Project 2: Data Analysis for Engineering Decisions

children.value: ENGR 132 - Transforming Ideas to Innovation II

A hands-on lab series teaching students to collect, analyze, and visualize data to inform engineering decisions. Students work with real datasets to explore statistical concepts and communicate findings.
Apply statistical methods to engineering problems
requiring comprehensive data analysis and reporting
for technical work and written communication
— Real engineering datasets from industry and research
Improved student confidence in data analysis skills (pre/post surveys)
High completion rates (>95%) on challenging projects
Materials adapted for other STEM courses

Interactive materials integrating engineering ethics and design thinking into problem-solving activities. Students analyze case studies, debate ethical dilemmas, and apply human-centered design principles.
Identify ethical considerations in engineering practice
Apply ethical frameworks to complex scenarios
Use empathy and iteration in design processes
based on real engineering ethical dilemmas
Enhanced student awareness of engineering’s societal impact
Positive instructor feedback on discussion quality
Comprehensive resources helping students develop technical communication skills essential for engineering practice. Includes writing guides, templates, and peer review processes.
Write clear technical reports and documentation
Create effective visual aids and figures
for lab write-ups and project deliverables
Improved writing quality across all assignments
Reduced grading time with clear rubrics
Students report increased confidence in technical writing
